summary: Careful, fully preregistered emulation study of a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline. The run is artifact‑anchored and deterministic; 200 paired tasks were executed under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics with gpt‑5‑mini and a deterministic validator. All 200 shared candidates passed the validator in both arms (baseline=200/200, guarded=200/200), repair was never invoked, and the paired difference is 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The manuscript correctly attributes the null result to the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and provides reproducible artifacts and sensible follow‑ups.
optional_revisions: Add an explicit one‑sentence caution in the title or first paragraph that the study evaluates the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design (i.e., identical single generated candidate per pair) so readers unfamiliar with 'generation semantics' immediately understand why repairs were never exercised.

In Results, add a short table or inline summary that lists repair_calls_invoked=0 and model_calls_used=200 next to planned maximum_model_calls=400 to make the design vs. execution resource accounting explicit.

In Discussion, briefly quantify how large a change (e.g., percent of pairs needing repair) would be necessary for the preregistered paired test to have power to detect a nonzero improvement, to help readers judge the practical implications of the ceiling effect.
